title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court concerning the Validity of Joint Operation Agreements Signed between Township Governments and Other Entities

articles.content_en: I. A joint venture agreement entered into in the name of a township government that has not yet separated government functions from enterprise management after the issuance of Document No. 6 (1986) of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council, i.e., the Provisions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Further Prohibiting Party and Government Organs and Their Cadres from Engaging in Commerce or Running Enterprises, shall be deemed as the township government exercising the dual functions of government and the township cooperative economic organization. If there is no illegal circumstance, it may not be treated as an invalid agreement. Where the agreement needs to be further performed, the joint venture entity shall be promptly changed in accordance with the progress of separating government functions from enterprise management, and all legal formalities shall be completed.

II. For a township government that has already separated government functions from enterprise management after Document No. 6 (1986), a joint venture agreement entered into still with the township government as one party shall, in principle, be found invalid in accordance with the provisions of Document No. 6 (1986). However, in adjudication practice, attention shall be paid to specific analysis of specific circumstances. If the joint venture agreement, although entered into in the name of the township government, is actually executed by the township cooperative economic organization, and the content of the agreement does not violate relevant laws or policies, and treating it as an invalid agreement would be detrimental to economic development, it may not be treated as an invalid agreement. Where the agreement needs to be further performed, the joint venture entity shall be changed, and all legal formalities shall be completed.

This is hereby replied.

January 9, 1988
